outcome: Contributing factors to maternal death (late referral, delays in managing PPH, inadequate preparations for PPH, delay in performing caesarean section)
cohort: 61 women who died of pregnancy-related complications at Dodoma Regional Referral Hospital (DRRH) between January 2018 and December 2019, of whom 23 died of obstetric haemorrhage
finding: Late referral, delays in managing postpartum hemorrhage, and inadequate preparation for high-risk pregnancies are major contributing factors to high maternal mortality from obstetric hemorrhage.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was the most common mode of delivery (52%) among women who died of obstetric haemorrhage, followed by laparotomy due to ruptured uterus (35%).
